subject: Request: credit allocation after July 24 EU partial degradation (EdgeScale)
messages:
From: Olivia Barnes <olivia@edgescale.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, EdgeScale Billing <billing@edgescale.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2027 21:22:00 +0000
Subject: Partial degradation in EU on Jul 24 — request for full credit

Hi Jonas,

On Jul 24 between ~02:13 and 02:47 UTC we observed an elevated error rate and tail latency on requests routed to Redwood's eu-west inference tier for our production routing key (edgescale-prod). Our internal monitoring shows ~12% of user requests failed or timed out for the 34-minute window; this materially impacted our SLAs to our end customers.

We received a maintenance notice from FastCDN (attached) that they were applying configuration changes to TLS handoff in the eu-west POPs during this window; however, our traffic was routed through Redwood's edge and we expected Redwood to absorb or route around upstream degradation. Given the impact, EdgeScale is requesting a full uptime credit for the incident window under Section 3.2 of the SLA.

Attachments: edgeprobe-eu-trace-2027-07-24.log (request traces), fastcdn-maintenance-notice-2027-07-24.pdf

Could you confirm Redwood's attribution and provide the credit calc and timeline?

Thanks,
Olivia Barnes
Head of Reliability, EdgeScale
olivia@edgescale.com

Team — forwarding EdgeScale's request. Quick notes:

- EdgeScale is asking for a full credit for the 34m window. They point to FastCDN's maintenance notice.
- Our initial telemetry (attached incident timeline draft) shows we had elevated retries at the edge for ~21m that correlate with FastCDN upstream errors, and a shorter ~13m window with increased queueing inside our tokenizer/route cluster that looks internal.
- SLA language (3.2) covers third-party upstreams in some cases (see section 3.2.c: "outages clearly attributable to third-party providers may be excluded"). We need a defensible, reproducible allocation method if we don't give full credit.

Action items:
1) Marissa — please review contract language and confirm whether we have to apply a full credit if customer cannot prove our control failure.
2) Rishi — can you pull raw probe logs and the route-level latency histograms for the eu-west route for 02:00–03:00 UTC? I want exact timing and an estimate of request fraction affected that we consider 'internal'.
3) I'll draft a customer-facing note that proposes a shared-responsibility credit if telemetry supports split responsibility.

I'll attach the draft timeline and the customer's trace file.

Thanks,
Jonas

Subject: RE: Partial degradation in EU on Jul 24 — request for full credit

Hi Olivia — thanks for the report and the traces. We completed an initial internal review and wanted to share our findings and a proposed remediation/credit approach.

Summary of findings
- Total customer-observed impact window: 02:13–02:47 UTC (34 minutes).
- FastCDN maintenance notice indicates config rollout in eu-west POPs overlapping 02:10–02:40 UTC. Their ops team confirmed increased TLS handshake failures stretching to 02:41 UTC.
- Redwood telemetry: three distinct behaviors observed in the eu-west path:
  1) 02:13–02:34 UTC — increased 502/504 responses at the edge that correlate directly with FastCDN handshake failures (~21 minutes).
  2) 02:34–02:47 UTC — a smaller window (~13 minutes) where internal queueing and worker retries increased due to backpressure; these traces show tokenization latency spikes inside our route pool and cannot be explained by FastCDN alone.

Allocation rationale
Given the telemetry, we cannot attribute the whole window solely to FastCDN. We propose attributing the 21-minute segment to third-party upstream (FastCDN) and the 13-minute segment to Redwood internal performance (queueing and retries). That yields a split of ~62% third-party / 38% Redwood responsibility for the customer-visible degradation.

Proposed customer remedy
- We propose issuing an uptime credit equal to 50% of the prorated invoice for the affected billing period (a compromise reflecting shared responsibility and the operational impact).
- We will also provide the raw route-level histograms and the incident timeline (link below) for audit.
- Operational follow-ups: we will enable additional routing failover logic for the eu-west POPs and add a short-term increase in probe fanout during vendor maintenance windows.

If EdgeScale prefers a different split, we can escalate to Legal for contract interpretation, but we wanted to offer this pragmatic option to resolve quickly.

Attachments: redwood-incident-timeline-draft.docx
Related link: https://drive.redwood/incident/INC-2027-324

Best,
Jonas
